petitionText:
You can sign two petitions. One to preserve the track in Kessel-Lo and restore it sustainably (under the authority of the Province of Flemish Brabant), and one to urge the City of Leuven to provide a new 200m track in or around Leuven (see 'Our story' above to read the justification for this). You do not have to choose; feel free to sign both petitions.
Thank you very much for supporting everyone involved!
petitionButton1: Sign to preserve the Kessel-Lo track
petitionButton2: Sign for a new 200m track in Leuven
welcome: Please help us to save our sport and track.

story.title: Our story
story.body1a: We need your help. Our beloved track has been badly neglected in recent years and is at risk of being replaced by an event space. The fear that the track will disappear quietly is very real. At first glance, it is just a large concrete structure, but what exactly is it that we could lose?
story.body1b: It is, at least, a place where people young and old try roller-skating or inline skating for the first time. Where couples had their first date, riding hand in hand. You can also find people who want to try something different, such as ski-rollers or elliptical bikes.
story.body1c: It is a place where you can freely and safely experiment with all kinds of transportation. Without cars or other heavy traffic. But it is more, it was more.
story.body1d: In the 1980s, Annie Lambrechts broke several world records; she was named sportswoman of the year in 1981 (source: Wikipedia). It is therefore part of the history of Groot-Leuven. It is also the place where Bart Swings laid the foundation for future successes and dreamed of an Olympic medal.
story.body1e: It is precisely those dreams and that sporting history that are in danger of being wiped away. The dreams of the next generation of Leuven skaters are also at serious risk. For now, they have to go to Tienen to train or try to make the best of the public roads, but that is far from an ideal solution. If it is a solution at all.
story.body1f: It was supposed to be temporary, but it threatens to become permanent. In that situation, there is no perspective; many skaters drop out or simply do not make the step to competition. At the very least, we need a place where they can train safely.
story.body2a: But that is not enough. For years, inline skating races have been held on a smaller 200m track. This means that Roll&Skate members should also train on the same type of track on which international competitions are held.
story.body2b: Inline skating is a highly technical sport. A 200m track has shorter (banked) bends, and you can easily maintain speeds of 40 km/h. There are a few 200m tracks in Belgium, but not very many. The best known are Zemst, Tienen and Ostend. Especially the latter is the pride of inline skating in Belgium.
story.body2c: Two years ago, the European Championship was organized in Ostend (Zandvoorde), and a European competition is held there every year. A highlight for our sport. A track like the one in Zandvoorde would not look out of place in a Leuven that wants to profile itself as a city for top-level sport. The city that has produced one of the best skaters ever deserves this.
story.body2d: Athletes like Bart Swings can remain the figurehead of our sport, of a track and of a tournament for years to come. Bart already brings a lot of international talent to Leuven, and in this way Leuven can become the cradle of our sport. Unfortunately, this is not recognized by the city council. For years, it has been blind to what our sport can mean, means and has meant for our beautiful city. That is a great pity. We therefore ask for your help to change this.
